title.narrative: OUTPUT 1.1 Integrated Landuse, Environment Management and Sustainable Development Plan developed for Gonarezhou National Park and Neighboring Communities

description.narrative: Holistic landuse planning and management is fundamental to ensuring socioecological resilience in the longterm and provides the basis for optimal management of space and natural resources with a view to maximizing overall productivity / livelihood support while ensuring ecological sustainability, provision of ecosystem services, mitigation of resource degradation and climate change, and mitigation of potential adverse impacts of mixed landuses on one another.The Action will employ and adapt existing sustainable development and resilience planning tools for participatory problem analysis, planning and action in creation of resilience in complex socioecological systems. This structured and comprehensively participatory approach will form the basis of individual Community Resilience Plans, which in turn will contribute to an overall landscapelevel LandUse and Environment Management Plan at District and TFCA levels. Community Resilience Plans will prioritize key interventions to promote greater social, livelihood, and ecological prosperity and resilience which will inform Resilience Fund investments under Output 2.5 of this Action.

description.narrative: Human Wildlife Conflict (HWC) is a multifactorial problem. Haphazard land use planning and improper agricultural practice and livestock husbandry are among the most important drivers of HWC. The Intervention will therefor focus on more appropriate land use planning and promoting increased awareness and training in HWC mitigation measures.The indicator will attempt to measure % reduction in HWC incidents in instances where recommended Land Use Planning and HWC mitigation strategies have been adopted against cases in which such guidelines have been ignored.

comment.narrative: Because the drivers of HWC are incredibly complex and multifactorial e.g. drought land use zonation wildlife densities human densities poaching perverse incentives to name a few a targeted reduction of 50 is ambitious but achievable.

description.narrative: In as much as Sustainable Integrated Landscape Management is central to addressing the Triple Challenge of livelihood support, biodiversity conservation, provision of ecosystem services and climate change mitigation and adaptation for the approach to be adopted and effectively implemented there needs to be tangible benefit for communities right from the onset. Impoverished communities simply cannot be expected to support and implicitly subsidize an integrated landscape approach in the hope of realizing longterm benefits, which appear somewhat abstract and remote when juxtaposed to the urgent realities of individual survival. It is therefore imperative to develop the means for sustainable climatesmart income generation to support and incentivize SLM through formation of a Community Environment and Development Fund (or Resilience Fund) for long term support to livelihood diversification, creation of greeneconomy opportunities and through Payments for (measurable and audited) Ecosystem and Conservation Services (described in Output 2.5 below).

description.narrative: Of the 5 community sectors neighboring Gonarezhou National Park, 2 have formally constituted CommunityBasedOrganizations (CBOs) for administration and governance of CBNRM in their respective sectors including Jamanda Community Conservancy (established by SATWILD under the EUfunded WILD Programme) and the Malipati Development Trust (established by Cesvi, also under a previous EU Project). The other community sectors are more informally represented at community level but formal registration of balanced, accountable legal entities in all sectors is a main priority identified by preliminary stakeholder consultation and will be supported under this Action which will also create formal institutional links for better coordination between individual community sectors as well as with district and transboundary TFCA institutions and planning structures.

title.narrative: Percentage of grassroots civil society organizations (CSOs) comprising women and youth

description.narrative: Women and youth are typically underrepresented in CSOs and other platforms for civic discourse, planning, governance and development. The Project will therefor promote and track participation of women and youth in CSO committees, planning and development structures through the Implementation Period.

title.narrative: Governance, TORs, administration, systems, infrastructure & HR established for longterm support to CBOs & administration of the Community Environment and Development Fund (CEDF)

description.narrative: This activity is focused on organizational restructuring and capacitation of SATWILD to (i) establish a permanent presence in and service the intervention landscape and to (ii) administer the Community Environment and Development Fund (CEDF) in the long term.

comment.narrative: At present the project is administered as part of Sustainable Agriculture Technology SAT which is the parent organization of SATWILD. The intent is that SATWILD be restructured to be more autonomous to establish permanent presence and capacity in the intervention landscape and to administer the CEDF according to EU standards in the long term. SATWILD is in the process of restructuring for this purpose.

For SATWILD to achieve independent registration as a Private Voluntary Organization PVO will require support of local and national authorities responsible for the registration. Recent 2021 changes to the PVO Act have made this process more complex and subject to the discretion of the National PVO Registrar and Minister of Social Services. Protracted delays and hurdles are to be expected.
